meta.title: Chakra UI vs Mantine: Which to Choose in 2026?
meta.description: Chakra UI vs Mantine comparison: styling, components, theming, maintenance, and architecture trade-offs for product teams.

verdict: Choose Chakra UI if you prioritize a minimal, style-props-driven API, strong accessibility defaults, and a mature design system. Choose Mantine if you want a larger component set, built-in hooks, and advanced features like spotlight and notifications out of the box. Both are solid; the right pick depends on your team's preferences and project requirements.

comparison.toolA: Chakra UI offers a well-curated set of components covering common UI needs such as buttons, forms, modals, menus, and layout primitives like Box and Stack. The library emphasizes composability and consistent styling through its style props system, but it does not include as many specialized components as some alternatives. Additional components may require third-party libraries or custom builds.
comparison.toolB: Mantine provides a broader component collection, including advanced inputs, date pickers, rich text editors, carousels, and data tables, which can reduce the need for extra dependencies. Its component set is designed to be used together with consistent theming and accessibility considerations. The sheer number of components may increase bundle size if not tree-shaken properly, but Mantine supports tree-shaking.

comparison.toolA: Chakra UI uses a theme object with design tokens, semantic tokens, and component style overrides, making it straightforward to implement dark mode and custom design systems. The style props API allows rapid styling directly on components, which many teams find intuitive. However, deep customization sometimes requires understanding Chakra's theme structure and may involve more boilerplate for complex variants.
comparison.toolB: Mantine's theming system is built around CSS variables and a theme object with colors, spacing, and component defaults, and it supports automatic dark mode. It provides a wide range of customization options, including component-level styles and CSS modules, which can be more flexible for teams comfortable with CSS. The learning curve for advanced theming may be slightly steeper due to the many configuration options.

comparison.toolA: Chakra UI places a strong emphasis on accessibility, with many components following WAI-ARIA guidelines and including keyboard navigation and focus management by default. It also provides support for right-to-left (RTL) layouts through its theme and components. That said, developers still need to test and ensure accessibility in their specific implementations.
comparison.toolB: Mantine also prioritizes accessibility, with components designed to meet WCAG standards and support keyboard navigation, ARIA attributes, and focus trapping where appropriate. It offers RTL support and includes utilities for managing focus and screen reader announcements. As with any library, final accessibility depends on correct usage and testing.

comparison.toolA: Chakra UI is written in TypeScript and provides strong type definitions for its components and theme, which helps catch errors during development. The style props system is fully typed, and the API is generally consistent and predictable. Some complex customizations may require type augmentation, but the overall developer experience is smooth for TypeScript users.
comparison.toolB: Mantine is also built with TypeScript and offers excellent type safety, including typed theme objects and component props. It provides a rich set of hooks and utilities that are fully typed, enhancing developer productivity. The documentation includes TypeScript examples, making it easy to get started.

comparison.toolA: Chakra UI's bundle size depends on the components used, and it supports tree-shaking to some extent, but its style props approach can lead to larger runtime CSS-in-JS overhead. Performance is generally good for typical applications, but very large or performance-critical apps may need to consider optimization techniques. The library has been improving performance over time.
comparison.toolB: Mantine is designed with performance in mind, using CSS variables and static CSS where possible, which can reduce runtime overhead. It supports tree-shaking and code-splitting, and its components are generally lightweight. However, including many components can increase bundle size, so proper configuration is important.

comparison.toolA: Chakra UI has a mature ecosystem with a dedicated community, regular updates, and comprehensive documentation that includes guides and examples. It has been around for several years and is widely adopted, which means many third-party resources and integrations are available. The maintainers are active and responsive to issues.
comparison.toolB: Mantine has a rapidly growing ecosystem with extensive documentation, a friendly community, and frequent releases. It offers additional packages like @mantine/hooks and @mantine/notifications that extend functionality. While its community may be smaller than Chakra's, it is highly active and supportive.

comparison.category: Learning curve and ease of adoption
comparison.toolA: Chakra UI is known for its gentle learning curve, especially for developers familiar with React and CSS-in-JS. The style props system allows quick prototyping, and the component APIs are intuitive. However, mastering the theming system and advanced patterns may take time.
comparison.toolB: Mantine's learning curve is moderate; its components are easy to use, but the extensive API and configuration options can be overwhelming for beginners. The documentation is thorough, which helps, but developers may need to spend more time exploring features. Teams with CSS experience may find it more approachable.

faq.q: Which library is better for a large-scale enterprise application?
faq.a: Both Chakra UI and Mantine can scale to enterprise applications, but the choice depends on your specific needs. Mantine's broader component set and built-in hooks may reduce development time for complex features, while Chakra UI's focused API and strong accessibility defaults can simplify design system maintenance. Consider factors like bundle size, theming requirements, and team familiarity with each library's patterns.

faq.q: Does Mantine support server-side rendering (SSR) and Next.js?
faq.a: Yes, Mantine supports server-side rendering and provides guidance for integrating with Next.js. Its components are designed to work with SSR, and the documentation includes examples for setting up Mantine in Next.js projects, including handling color schemes and CSS variables. However, as with any library, you should test your specific setup to ensure compatibility.

faq.q: Is Chakra UI still actively maintained in 2026?
faq.a: Chakra UI has a history of active maintenance and regular releases, and as of 2026 it continues to be developed by its maintainers. However, the exact release cadence and roadmap can vary, so it's advisable to check the official repository and changelog for the latest information. The library has a stable community and is used in many production applications.

faq.q: Which library has better support for dark mode?
faq.a: Both Chakra UI and Mantine offer built-in dark mode support with easy toggling. Chakra UI uses its color mode script and theme tokens, while Mantine uses CSS variables and a color scheme provider. The implementation differs, but both are effective; your choice may depend on which API you find more intuitive.

faq.q: Can I use Chakra UI and Mantine together in the same project?
faq.a: Technically, it is possible to use both libraries in the same project, but it is generally not recommended due to potential conflicts in styling, theming, and bundle size. Mixing two UI libraries can lead to inconsistent design and increased complexity. It's better to choose one based on your project's requirements and stick with it for consistency.

faq.q: Which library is more performant for small, static sites?
faq.a: For small, static sites, performance differences may be negligible. Mantine's use of CSS variables and static CSS can reduce runtime overhead, while Chakra UI's style props may introduce some CSS-in-JS overhead. However, both libraries support tree-shaking, so the actual impact depends on how many components you use and your build configuration. Always measure performance in your specific context.

faq.q: How do the licensing terms compare?
faq.a: Both Chakra UI and Mantine are open-source libraries released under the MIT license, which allows free use in commercial and personal projects. You should review the license files in their respective repositories to confirm, but generally, both are permissive and suitable for most applications.

faq.q: Which library is better for a team new to React?
faq.a: Chakra UI's simpler API and style props system may be easier for teams new to React to pick up quickly, as it reduces the need to write separate CSS files. Mantine's extensive feature set might be overwhelming initially, but its documentation is excellent. Consider your team's background: if they are comfortable with CSS and want more out-of-the-box features, Mantine could work; if they prefer a gentle learning curve, Chakra UI might be a better fit.
